name: Jules Bordet
summary: Belgian immunologist and Nobel laureate known for discovering complement and Bordetella pertussis.

name: Elie Metchnikoff
summary: Russian biologist and mentor to Bordet, champion of cellular immunity.

name: Octave Gengou
summary: Belgian bacteriologist and collaborator of Bordet.

name: Paul Ehrlich
summary: German immunologist and rival of Bordet, originator of side-chain theory.

name: Pasteur Institute
summary: Research institute in Paris where Bordet began his groundbreaking experiments.

name: Free University of Brussels
summary: University in Brussels where Bordet enrolled in medical school and later taught.

name: Pasteur Institute of Brussels
summary: Institute in Brussels directed by Bordet after his return from Paris.

name: League of Nations
summary: International organization Bordet lobbied regarding poison gas.

name: Soignies
summary: Small town in Belgium where Bordet was born.

name: Brussels
summary: City in Belgium where Bordet's family moved and where he worked.

name: complement
summary: Heat-labile substance in serum enabling bacteria-killing ability, termed 'alexin' by Bordet.

name: complement fixation test
summary: Serologic assay developed by Bordet and Gengou to detect antibodies.

name: Bordetella pertussis
aliases: organism responsible for causing whooping cough
summary: Organism responsible for whooping cough, cultured by Bordet and Gengou.

name: Nobel Prize in Medicine or Physiology
summary: Award given to Bordet for discoveries relating to immunity.
